contentPolicy.notes: These two commands return a Promise of the ordinary JSON-string reply envelope. Runtime.evaluate must use awaitPromise:true and returnByValue:true. getContentPolicy answers from the current snapshot WITHOUT waiting on a pending read: while the mirror is not yet applied it replies {ok:false,error:'contentPolicyUnavailable'} immediately, which is retryable, rather than holding the promise open. setContentPolicy resolves only once the write is durable. active:true means a policy is applied AND durable; active:false with playback continuing means the mirror could not be read and the built-in default (mature hidden, everything else plays) is in force until a later read or setContentPolicy succeeds — the daemon should repair it. Malformed policy returns invalidContentPolicy. blockUnratedCurated is an operator audit gate, not a controller setting. Missing cast contentContext means curated. contentRating is an OPEN vocabulary (dp1 3.3): only 'mature' hides anything, and any other string reads as unrated, so no document is refused and no item hidden over a label the player cannot read. This is a convenience viewing default, not tamper-resistant parental control.

recentlyPlayed.notes: getRecentlyPlayed {} returns {ok,status,records,incomplete,activeOccurrenceKnown}. status is 'ok', 'empty' when nothing is retained, or 'error' with an explicit message — an unknown command or a transport failure must never be read as an empty history. Before the store has been read the reply is {ok:false,status:'error',error:'Recently played is still loading'}; the player reads it at boot so a controller should not normally see that. records[].isActive marks the retained record that is on screen NOW. activeOccurrenceKnown false means the device cannot yet say whether one is (a work committing, a restart before the first commit, or a failed render until a later commit, a stop, or a cast with nothing to show) — treat it as pending, not as 'nothing has ever played'. true with no record active means none is on screen: a stop, sleep, a policy change that moved the selection, or a work too large to retain. incomplete true means a committed work is missing from the timeline, including when the store itself was unreadable and was started over. resolveRecentlyPlayed {recordId} is INTERNAL to controld: it returns the retained item plus its defaults and contentContext so controld can re-enter its ordinary displayPlaylist path, which is what retires displayAt scheduler ownership. Do not treat it as a play command; there is no player-local replay. An evicted or malformed recordId is rejected before anything on the wall changes.

displayPlaylistPolicy.notes: displayPlaylist.request.contentContext is 'curated' | 'personal', outside the signed DP-1 body. Absent means curated on a new cast; on a refresh it means UNCHANGED and inherits the cast's own origin, an explicit 'curated' narrows, and an explicit 'personal' is honoured only when the cast is already personal — a refresh can never invent a personal origin. checkStatus echoes the applied contentContext. retireBlockedCurrent:true is controld's refresh-only hint that it has already removed the blocked item from its own projection, so the current work must retire immediately instead of finishing its slot. contentBlocked means policy left nothing playable in the cast and the current work was NOT replaced; an empty item list is not contentBlocked, it clears playback. playlistInvalid means malformed input — a contentRating that is not a string, or a malformed contentReasons — and never an unrecognised rating value.

setupDisplay.notes: Requests missing a required field for their state are rejected with {ok:false}. progress must be a finite number. The player renders overlay-driving commands (mintPairingDisplay, setupDisplay) without arbitration, so the controller must keep at most one non-hidden at a time.

renderStatus.notes: checkStatus replies carry an optional numeric renderStatus: 0 pending, 1 loading, 2 ready, 3 failed. Live-only — never persisted, so boot and hydrate strip it. `ready` means the artwork finished loading AND is what the screen is showing, not that it rendered correctly. It publishes when the incoming slot commits, so on a transition it trails byte arrival by up to the crossfade duration (650ms); a first load publishes immediately. For iframe/PDF a browser-generated error document still reports ready, because Chromium does not emit an iframe error for a failed navigation. On a player build that declares this entry, an ABSENT renderStatus means 'no lifecycle published yet for the current mount' — not a terminal state, and not a fault. A manifest without this entry is an older build that never reports the field at all: controld must treat that as capability-absent rather than as a stuck pending, because the two are byte-identical on the wire (JSON.stringify drops the undefined key).

playerStatus.notes: window.__ffosPlayerStatus() (no request payload — a plain global function, not a checkStatus-style command) returns JSON.stringify({protocol, route, handlerRegistered, hasArtwork, bootHydration}), where bootHydration is one of pending|ok|halted_cleared|halted_preserving|failed. Installed by CDPRequestHandler.initialize() and set back to null by cleanup(). Absent on player builds that predate this contract entry — controld's capability fuse treats a manifest without this entry as unsupported and falls back to conservative (log-only) boot recovery.

mediaHealth.notes: Paired with feral-controld's mediahealth store (ffos-user#392). HINTS: displayPlaylist.request.mediaHealth is a sparse object keyed by item.source as pushed, broken entries only, each {category, reason}; it rides beside dp1_call on every push (cast, boot cast, refresh) and the signed DP-1 body is untouched. Absent means NO hints, on a refresh too (unlike contentContext, which inherits): a controld that declares this entry sends the map on every push. The timeline resolves every selection past hinted sources BEFORE mounting, in play order; `playlist` wraps, `none` does not, and `one` ignores hints because the viewer asked for that work. Hinted items stay in checkStatus.items; the published index is where playback actually landed. When nothing else is playable (an all-broken map, or only hinted works remain under repeat-off) the requested slot plays anyway and the ordinary 3-attempt retry/skip budget judges it, so a hint can never blank the wall. Hints are never persisted: after a reboot the next push restores them. Malformed maps are ignored, never rejected. HINT SKIPS: checkStatus.skippedIndices is an array of indices into checkStatus.items that the player is passing over because of a hint it HOLDS, ascending, ALWAYS present from this player ([] when nothing is hinted or nothing is cast). It is the player's state, not controld's observation: copy it per item into player_status.mediaHealth[i].skipped (absent from an older build means false). It follows the selection rules above: [] under `one`; under `playlist` every hinted slot while any unhinted slot exists; under `none` only a hinted slot with an unhinted slot after it (the tolerated tail still plays); [] when every slot is hinted. The published index is never listed: the work on the wall is not being skipped, including one whose hint arrived on a refresh mid-play (it is listed once playback leaves it). Recomputed on every status read, so a push that drops or adds a hint shows on the next poll. OUTCOMES: checkStatus.outcomes is {castSeq, entries[]}, ALWAYS present from this player ({castSeq:0, entries:[]} before anything reports; an older build omits the key). entries are oldest-first, at most 64, each {seq, castSeq, source, kind, stage, code?, mediaType?, attempt, elapsedMs, at}. The outer castSeq is the CURRENT generation: it increments on every accepted Now Display (explicit, boot replay, scheduled, fallback). Each entry carries the castSeq it was recorded under and keeps it for as long as it is retained, so dedupe by the ENTRY's (castSeq, seq), never by the outer castSeq paired with seq: an undrained failure from cast 1 is still (1, n) after cast 2 opens and must not count as corroboration from a distinct cast. seq is monotonic for the PAGE lifetime and is never reset per cast, so dedupe by seq alone is equivalent. Both restart with the page: a drained seq lower than the last one seen means the player restarted, so controld must restart its dedupe rather than drop the entries. Nothing is removed on read; controld reads a seq jump as a gap. Stages: detect = the content-type HEAD probe answered non-2xx (code = HTTP status) or failed with corroborated offline (code = network); the iframe fallback still plays the work, so a detect fail can be followed by an ok in the SAME play and entries must be applied in seq order. load = an element error (code = image|video|audio|iframe|object|model, or hls_<hls.js ErrorType> for a fatal HLS error). decode = a video/audio MediaError (code = aborted|network|decode|src_not_supported). watchdog = the per-slot stuck-load watchdog expired (code = the load phase that ran out: transfer, no bytes for its idle bound or past the transfer ceiling; decode, bytes complete but the element never reported; opaque, a plain element load with no visible progress; fixed, iframe/object/model/PDF, which expose none). webgl = GPU context lost on the probe canvas (code = context_lost): device-local, never a source verdict. exhausted = the retry budget is spent (code = attempt limit); the playlist then advances. hint = kind skip, the timeline honoured a hint and never mounted the source (attempt 0, elapsedMs 0). ready = kind ok, the mount reached ready; elapsedMs is mount to ready. One fail entry per attempt: competing failure signals for the same attempt are collapsed at the transition into failed. attempt is 1-based within the per-item budget and resets on a new work or a genuine success. mediaType is the resolved renderer (image|video|audio|iframe|pdf|object|model) once MIME detection settled, absent before. Source URLs appear here only over loopback CDP; the player never sends them anywhere else.
